Read the states of a lag sequential analysis fit

Source: R/tidy-accessors.R
nodes.Rd

nodes() returns the states of a lag sequential analysis fit, one row per state with its total outgoing and incoming transition counts. In a lag transition network the states are the nodes, and how often a state is left and how often it is entered describe its place in the process: a state with many outgoing but few incoming transitions tends to open episodes, one with the reverse tends to close them. The marginal totals also set the expected counts against which every transition is tested.

The shares of all transitions and the initial-state probability are in as.data.frame(summary(fit), what = "nodes"); the per-transition table is transitions().

Usage

nodes(fit)

# S3 method for class 'lsa'
nodes(fit)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_group'
nodes(fit)

Arguments

fit

An lsa fit from lsa(), or a grouped fit from lsa(..., group = ).

Value

A data.frame with one row per state and the columns state (matching the from and to names of transitions()), outgoing and incoming. A grouped fit gives one row per group and state, with a leading group column.

See also

transitions(), initial(), tests(), lsa-methods for summary().

Examples

nodes(lsa(engagement))
#>        state outgoing incoming
#> 1     Active      658      651
#> 2    Average      751      763
#> 3 Disengaged      325      320
